markers.title: Day-nav arrows are too small to tap
markers.body: The ‹ and › date-scroll arrows are only ~9×26dp — far below the 44×44dp minimum touch target. Widen the tappable area (padding, not just glyph size) even if the visual chevron stays small.

markers.title: 'Today' and '+ Add' buttons undersized
markers.body: Both header buttons render as ~40×17dp text labels with no extra hit-slop. Increase the button height to at least 44dp so front-desk staff can tap reliably while multitasking.

markers.title: Inconsistent row heights break grid rhythm
markers.body: Suite 1 and Suite 2 rows are only 18dp tall while every other room row (including Suite 3-5) is 36dp. This misaligns the room-label column against the booking grid and creates uneven vertical rhythm — normalize all room rows to the same height.

markers.title: Room-label column too narrow for longer names
markers.body: The fixed 45dp-wide label column works for 'Room 1' but is cramped for names like 'Family Room 7'. Long labels risk wrapping awkwardly or truncating to unreadable fragments — widen the column or truncate with a full-name tooltip/press-and-hold.

markers.title: 'Unallocated (N) ›' row control has a short tap height
markers.body: The room-type header row (e.g. 'Bridge Room … Unallocated (10) ›') that likely expands the unallocated list is only ~17dp tall. Even though it spans the row's full width, its vertical hit area is too small — pad the whole header row to ≥44dp of tappable height.

markers.title: Shaded date-range band has no legend
markers.body: A pink/salmon highlight covers a block of days and rooms with no caption, icon, or legend explaining what it represents (e.g. blocked, held, or booked dates). Add a label or key so the meaning isn't colour-only.

working_well: Day columns pair the weekday abbreviation with the date number, making the horizontal timeline easy to scan.
Grouping rooms under clear category headers (Bridge Room, Deluxe Suite, Family Room) gives the long room list a useful hierarchy.
Surfacing the 'Unallocated (N)' count directly in each room-type header helps staff spot unassigned bookings without digging into the grid.
Room numbering is sequential and consistent, so staff can quickly map rows to physical rooms.
worth_considering: A sticky room-label column while scrolling horizontally through dates would help staff keep track of which row they're viewing.
A quick 'jump to date' control alongside the arrows would speed up navigating far-future or past dates.
Consider a compact legend chip for the shaded booking states so colour meaning is discoverable at a glance.
Grouping the 'Today' pill and '+ Add' action with a touch of extra spacing would reduce accidental mis-taps between them.
